title: Review: Counting particles by mass: The mole
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S1.4#c07 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S1.4.5#xt3 term and clue written for the game; S1.4.5#xt1 term and clue written for the game; S1.4.6#xt1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: S1.4#q02, S1.4#q04, S1.4#q06, S1.4#q09, S1.4#q13, S1.4#q15, S1.4#q01, S1.4#q18, S1.4#q07, S1.4#q10, S1.4#q14, S1.4#q17. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Molar mass, M
items.clue: Grams of a substance per 6.02 × 10²³ of its specified particles.

items.label: Solute
items.clue: The dissolved substance, such as NaCl in brine, whose amount is n in n = CV.

items.label: Molar concentration
items.clue: Amount of dissolved substance per unit volume, written with square brackets, e.g. [NaCl].

items.label: Avogadro's law
items.clue: Equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in 0.500 mol of water, H₂O? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Each H₂O molecule has 3 atoms. Atoms = 0.500 mol × 3 × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 9.03 × 10²³.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'M_r of carbon dioxide, CO₂ = 44.01 g mol⁻¹'. Which comment on this statement is correct?

options.text: It is correct: M_r and molar mass are one and the same quantity.
The unit is wrong: M_r is the mass of one molecule in grams.
The unit is wrong: M_r is measured in atomic mass units.
The unit is wrong: M_r is a ratio of masses, with no unit.

questions.explanation: M_r compares the mass of a CO₂ molecule with one twelfth of the mass of a ¹²C atom, so the units cancel: M_r(CO₂) = 44.01. The quantity with unit g mol⁻¹ is the molar mass, M(CO₂) = 44.01 g mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: How many ions are there in 5.55 g of calcium chloride, CaCl₂? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; A_r: Cl 35.45, Ca 40.08)
questions.explanation: M(CaCl₂) = 40.08 + 2 × 35.45 = 110.98 g mol⁻¹; n = 5.55 ÷ 110.98 = 0.0500 mol. Each formula unit contains 3 ions (one Ca²⁺, two Cl⁻): 0.0500 × 3 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 9.03 × 10²².

questions.stem: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄? (A_r: H 1.01, N 14.01, O 16.00, S 32.07)
Which procedure produces a solution in which [NaCl] = 0.500 mol dm⁻³? (M(NaCl) = 58.44 g mol⁻¹)

options.text: Add 0.125 mol of NaCl to 250 cm³ of water and stir until dissolved.
Dissolve 2.92 g of NaCl and make up to 100 cm³ of solution.
Dissolve 0.500 g of NaCl, then make the solution up to 1.00 dm³.
Add 0.500 mol of NaCl to 250 cm³ of water and stir to dissolve it.

questions.explanation: [NaCl] = 0.500 mol dm⁻³ corresponds to 0.500 × 58.44 = 29.2 g dm⁻³; 100 cm³ of solution therefore needs 2.92 g (0.0500 mol), made up to the mark in a volumetric flask.

questions.stem: Two identical sealed flasks are at the same temperature and pressure. One is filled with methane, CH₄, and the other with chlorine, Cl₂. The methane flask contains 5.00 × 10²² atoms in total. How many atoms does the chlorine flask contain? (A_r: H 1.01, C 12.01, Cl 35.45)
questions.explanation: Equal volumes at the same T and p contain equal numbers of molecules. The CH₄ flask holds 5.00 × 10²² ÷ 5 = 1.00 × 10²² molecules, so the Cl₂ flask also holds 1.00 × 10²² molecules, which contain 2 × 1.00 × 10²² = 2.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Which statement about one mole of a substance is correct?

options.text: It contains 6.02 × 10²³ of whichever entity is specified.
It has a mass of 12 g, whichever substance it may be.
It contains 6.02 × 10²³ atoms, whatever the substance.
It occupies 22.7 dm³ at 273.15 K and 100 kPa, whatever its state.

questions.explanation: One mole contains N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ elementary entities, and the entity must be named: 1 mol of H₂O is 6.02 × 10²³ molecules but 3 × 6.02 × 10²³ atoms.

questions.stem: What is the relative formula mass, M_r, of hydrated calcium nitrate, Ca(NO₃)₂·4H₂O? (A_r: H 1.01, N 14.01, O 16.00, Ca 40.08)
questions.explanation: Add every atom, including the four water molecules: 40.08 + 2(14.01 + 3 × 16.00) + 4(2 × 1.01 + 16.00) = 40.08 + 124.02 + 72.08 = 236.18. M_r has no unit.

questions.stem: The relative molecular mass of methane, CH₄, is 16.05. Which statement about the molar mass, M, of methane is correct?

options.text: It is 16.05 g; one molecule of CH₄ has a mass of 16.05 g.
It is 16.05, with no unit, as molar mass is the same as M_r.
It is 16.05 g mol⁻¹; 1 mol of CH₄ molecules has mass 16.05 g.
It is 16.05 g mol⁻¹; 16.05 g of CH₄ contains 6.02 × 10²³ atoms.

questions.explanation: Molar mass is mass per mole, in g mol⁻¹, and has the same number as M_r: 16.05 g is the mass of 1 mol (6.02 × 10²³) of CH₄ molecules, so M = 16.05 g mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: The empirical formula of ethanoic acid is CH₂O. What does this empirical formula tell you about ethanoic acid?

options.text: Its atoms of C, H and O are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.
Each of its molecules has one C atom, two H atoms and one O atom.
The masses of its C, H and O are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.
Each of its C atoms is bonded to two H atoms and to one O atom.

questions.explanation: The empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms: C₂H₄O₂ simplifies to 1 : 2 : 1, written CH₂O.

questions.stem: A solution of chlorine in water contains 4.00 g of dissolved chlorine, Cl₂, per dm³. Ignore any reaction of chlorine with water. What is [Cl₂]? (A_r: Cl 35.45)

options.text: 0.113 mol dm⁻³
284 mol dm⁻³
0.0564 mol dm⁻³
4.00 mol dm⁻³

questions.stem: At the same temperature and pressure, a flask holds 0.640 g of oxygen, O₂, when filled with oxygen and 1.28 g of gas X when filled with X. What is the molar mass of X? (A_r: O 16.00)

options.text: 32.0 g mol⁻¹
16.0 g mol⁻¹
64.0 g mol⁻¹
2.00 g mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: Equal volumes at the same T and p contain equal amounts: n = 0.640 g ÷ 32.00 g mol⁻¹ = 0.0200 mol. M(X) = 1.28 g ÷ 0.0200 mol = 64.0 g mol⁻¹.
